transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon. President Trump has cast his ballot in the midterm elections, saying he voted for all Republicans running in Florida.
Before he heads to Georgia, he'll be speaking at a rally there tonight.
Former President Obama is also on the campaign trail. He's been speaking out on behalf of Democrats running for office in Ohio and in Michigan.
In Alaska, the Democrat in the state's tight Senate race is among those asking a federal judge to throw out a Department of Justice lawsuit, which seeks to block the certification of the election if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses.
Alaska Public Media's Liz Ruskin has that story.
President Trump says he personally ordered the lawsuit. It would block Alaska from certifying a win by Democrat Mary Peltola pending an investigation to determine if voters were confused by a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, a retired teacher.
The ballot lists one Sullivan as the Republican incumbent, the other as Daniel J. Jr. with no party affiliation.
The senator's campaign says Alaskans can tell the difference. Still, the campaign said it would let the lawsuit run its course. Peltola calls the lawsuit corrupt.
As her attorneys put it, Trump insists Alaskans reelect the senator or he won't let them elect anyone at all.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
Ukraine says the satellite communication system Starlink and its Starshield technology is now fully functioning again. NPR's Polina Litvinova reports from Kyiv.
In his video address, President Zelensky said the disruptions were over at night and by the morning the speed was sufficient enough for communication service to work properly.
Starlink is crucial for Ukraine's military and defensive operations.
This really matters, Zelensky said, for our frontline logistics for defending Ukraine against jet-powered jet-head drones.
Last week, without warning, Ukraine lost the ability to use Starlink for these critical functions.
Even though now it's working again, the country is seeking for alternative satellite communications, not to rely only on American technology.
Polina Litvinova, NPR News, Kyiv.
Hundreds of people have been rescued from flooded homes along the San Juan River near Farmington, New Mexico since yesterday, following severe storms and flash flooding in the southwest.
San Juan County Fire Chief David Vega says crews are going door to door.
As the water's starting to recede in some areas, that's going to provide us an opportunity for us to get crews in, do a very slow, methodical search of all the houses to make sure that we haven't missed anything.
Chief Vega praises the work of the first responders, calling their efforts "heroic."
Flash flooding has also touched parts of Colorado, Arizona, and Utah.
You're listening to NPR.
A new survey shows the economy continues to be a major source of stress for most Americans, with nearly eight in ten reporting that the cost of living is the biggest stressor in their lives.
NPR's Rethu Chatterjee reports.
Financial pressures and concerns about the future of the country remain on top of people's minds, according to the latest annual Stress in America survey by the American Psychological Association, or the APA.
But six in ten adults also reported health care as a big source of stress.
Psychologist Vail Wright is senior director of health care innovation at the APA.
Nearly half of survey respondents also reported that stress is keeping them from participating in social activities.
Rethu Chatterjee, NPR News.
The U.S. has designated helium as a critical material.
Helium is used to make semiconductors, which are essential to energy generation, and is primarily produced as a byproduct of making natural gas.
The U.S. is the world's largest producer of natural gas and of helium.
Qatar and Russia are all the other top helium producers.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the Trump administration is freeing the U.S. from relying on foreign sources of critical materials and strengthening domestic production, which he says will support more American jobs, while it also helps to secure those essential materials like helium.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
This message comes from Aura. A data breach may have exposed more than 153 million driver's licenses in the U.S.
A breach like that doesn't wreck your life by itself, but when someone uses your information, the cleanup becomes your job.
That's what Aura is for. Aura alerts you fast if your info shows up in a breach, then locks your credit and provides U.S.-based fraud support 24/7.
You may not be able to stop all of it, but you can stop doing it alone.
Get started at aura.com/npr
